In sulphur estimation, $2.0 \times 10^{-3} \, \mathrm{mol}$ of an organic compound (X) (molar mass $76 \, \mathrm{g} \, \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$) gave 0.4813 g of barium sulphate (molar mass $233 \, \mathrm{g} \, \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$). The percentage of sulphur in the compound (X) is _____ $\times 10^{-1} \%$. (Nearest integer).
questions.solution:
Key idea: all the sulphur in the compound ends up as $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$. Since 1 mol $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$ contains 1 mol S: $\%S = \frac{32}{233}\times\frac{m_{BaSO_4}}{m_{compound}}\times100$
Mass of compound X: $m = 2.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{mol}\times76\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}} = 0.152\,\mathrm{g}$
Moles of $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$: $n = \frac{0.4813\,\mathrm{g}}{233\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}} = 2.0657\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{mol}$
